extracted.intended_audience: independent nonfiction/documentary filmmakers applying to the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/assessment criteria for submitting feature-length documentary grant applications to the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund, including required materials, priorities, and how proposals are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines and submission window
rubrics_metrics.description: The Documentary Fund accepts submissions through periodic open calls. Applicants must submit within the published open call dates (e.g., Feb 13–Apr 17, 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No deadline extensions are offered. Applicants are notified by fall/winter of the application year; decisions typically take six months. After submit, confirmation page and email will appear/arrive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project phase and readiness to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit only when you have written or visual material that demonstrates your creative and storytelling intent; you may submit at any production phase from development through post-production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All proposals must convey some vision for a finished film. Projects that have not yet secured characters/subjects, cannot articulate story or structure, or cannot explain the project's driving central question are discouraged. Story research proposals are ineligible. Apply at least six months before an anticipated premiere; picture-locked cuts are ineligible for post-production funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported film types and artistic standards
rubrics_metrics.description: We support cinematic documentaries embracing a wide range of aesthetic traditions and storytelling approaches and artists who demonstrate a clarity of vision, distinct voice, and meaningful connection to the story being told.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid/animated and experimental documentaries are eligible. The Fund prioritizes artistic clarity, distinct voice, and meaningful connection to subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible film types
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund does not fund fiction, short films (see Documentary Short Fund), series, NGO films, advocacy films, educational films, or branded content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purely historical or biographical films are generally not funded unless they show contemporary relevance or innovation in form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-length minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible projects must be feature-length documentaries (52 minutes and longer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget size priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The DFP prioritizes films with budgets under $1 million USD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not strictly excluding higher budgets, projects under $1M are prioritized in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative and editorial control
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative and editorial control must be held by members of the films’ key creative teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects eligibility and prioritization; demonstrate who holds creative/editorial authority in the team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization for U.S. productions
rubrics_metrics.description: For United States productions, the Fund prioritizes films led by artists from historically underrepresented communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects focusing on historically underrepresented communities must have a key creative from the community or with deep ties to the community in a power-holding position on the team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of historically underrepresented communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Communities historically marginalized by virtue of their ability, citizenship status, ethnicity, gender identity, race, religion, or sexual orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization for international productions
rubrics_metrics.description: For international productions, priority is given to films led by artists from Africa, China, India, Latin America, and the Middle East; indigenous artists globally and diaspora artists from these regions are also prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous Sundance Documentary Fund grantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects that have previously received a grant through the Documentary Fund are not eligible to apply for additional funding through this open call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact DFP staff for more information about exceptions or other options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive budget requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A budget covering the costs of the entire project from development through distribution is required for every funding category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a one- to two-page comprehensive line-item budget in U.S. dollars. Distinguish clearly between funds applied for and funds already secured. A sample PDF/Excel template is available but may be tailored; other formats acceptable if they provide the required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A fundraising strategy is required: a plan for raising the film budget including grants, broadcast license agreements, private donations, in-kind support, crowdfunding, producer investment, and fundraisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The strategy should clearly distinguish between funds applied for and funds already secured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of grant funds and ineligible uses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund does not fund film transfers, film prints, or debt reimbursement to complete work; generally does not provide solely completion funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-premiere support is not available; picture-locked cuts are ineligible for post-production funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual sample format and delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: All visual samples must be submitted as online streaming links (Vimeo or YouTube recommended); provide links and passwords if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use WeTransfer, Dropbox, Google Drive, or other file-transfer services; DVDs are not accepted except by special DVD exemption request when internet access is significantly impeded. Ensure the file/password is correct and available for at least six months after submission; do not change or update uploaded files/passwords after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual sample length per phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Development: encouraged (but not required) up to 15 minutes; Production: minimum of 10 minutes of edited footage required; Post-production: minimum of 20 minutes required. Sundance guarantees watching up to 30 minutes of visual material provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production or post-production proposals with very short reels (trailers/teasers/brief selects) are not competitive against longer samples and may instead be reviewed and considered in the development category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completed previous work sample requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed previous work may be any length and genre but should reflect the vision for the new project; reviewers will not review more than one previous work sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A visual sample that conveys the director’s creative perspective and ability to execute is preferred. For directorial debuts, you may submit a film you have shot or edited or choose not to submit a previous work. A previous work from a different member of the team (e.g., producer, editor, cinematographer) will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be written in English, visual materials must be in English or subtitled in English, and budgets must be translated into U.S. dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission and updates process
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply online only; after submission you will see a confirmation page and receive an email. Significant updates may be emailed to dfp@sundance.org but updates are not guaranteed to be incorporated into review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not call for application process inquiries; staff will not provide status updates and ask that applicants not contact about status. If additional information is needed, DFP staff will contact the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria used by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated on several criteria, including artful film language, engaging storytelling, originality, feasibility, contemporary cultural relevance, and potential to reach and connect with its intended audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Documentary Fund also prioritizes funding films from early-career and emerging artists; film teams’ experience level and access to resources (financial and creative) are taken into consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and reapply policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may reapply after a decline, but only when the project has advanced considerably in storytelling vision and intent and preferably at a later stage of production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filmmakers are strongly discouraged from resubmitting nearly identical proposals or visual samples. If reapplying, submit a brand-new online application with significant development and new video links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual and reporting requirements for grantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are not recoupable and do not encumber exploitable rights. To distribute funds, director and producer agreements and a clear chain of title are required. The Fund requests verbal and logo acknowledgment in end credits and promotional materials, a high-resolution digital copy of the film, and narrative, financial, and distribution reports (and social impact reports if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees may be requested to participate in Sundance Institute creative community activities. Grants are partial support; projects must seek additional funding and licensing/distribution agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition and funding rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process is highly competitive: approximately 1,100 proposals are reviewed each year and 30 to 40 films are funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates selectivity; present a compelling artistic and feasible project to be competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with festival and distribution opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving a Documentary Fund grant does not guarantee screening at the Sundance Film Festival; the Festival selects films independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving a Sundance Institute Documentary Fund grant does not preclude working with broadcasters or distributors.
